The contested zone is the ledger's contest event.

ledger.note: 1956: Soviet forces crush the revolution. "The second Soviet intervention, codenamed "Operation Whirlwind"" began at 03:00 on 4 November; "Soviet victory on 10 November" (lead; the infobox gives 11 November and the page says "outside of Budapest, firefights lasted until at least 12 November 1956"); Kádár became Prime Minister with most of Budapest under Soviet control by 8 November.

1989: the People's Republic ends on 23 October, the 33rd anniversary of the revolution. "One of Szűrös' first acts was to officially proclaim the Republic of Hungary"; "the Presidential Council was dissolved".

wars.name: Hungarian Revolution of 1956

union.text: Dunaújváros (coordinates; the place is not in the gazetteer)

zones.text: Budapest ("Soviet tanks penetrated Budapest along the Pest side of the Danube in two thrusts"), with resistance "in and around the city of Pécs in the Mecsek Mountains" and "the industrial centre of Dunaújváros"

wars.outcome: Soviet victory (infobox, 23 October - 11 November 1956): the Red Army occupied Budapest on 24 October, withdrew, and returned on 4 November; Kádár replaced Nagy. No frontier moved.
wars.note: The infobox "Belligerents" lists the revolutionaries and, from 24 October, the Nagy government against the Soviet Union and, from 4 November, the Kádár government. About 200,000 fled as refugees; sporadic resistance and strikes continued until mid-1957. The contest events fix the zone as Budapest, Pécs and Dunaújváros only; the page says that by treaty Hungary accepted the Soviet presence on a permanent basis afterwards, which is not drawn here as an occupation.

certainty.note: The whole frontier is the one fixed by the Paris peace treaty (signed 10 February 1947, in force 15 September 1947): the Trianon-era line with Romania and Yugoslavia and the loss of three villages near Bratislava to Czechoslovakia; no later change is dated by the pages opened.

notes: Three pages (budget up to 5). Overlap to settle: Cliopatria draws the Second Republic as the row "Hungary" 1947-1949 and this state as 1950-1989, but the People's Republic was promulgated on 20 August 1949; this dossier starts in 1949-08 and carries a 1949 keyframe from the Hungary row, so the hungary dossier (another part of eu-22) and this one overlap in the year 1949. Hungary has no shape for 1956-1957 in either row; a new keyframe covers it. Unexplained shape changes: 1969 (+89 km2) and none other; outline noise. Not events because the pages are silent or the change is not territorial: the Warsaw Pact accession (the page says only "member of the Warsaw Pact and Comecon"), admission to the UN on 14 December 1955, the opening of the Austrian border in 1989, the 12 October 1957 flag change, the Soviet troop presence (agreement of April 1989 to withdraw "by June 1991"). The Hungarian-Soviet frontier (Carpathian Ruthenia) is not dated by any page opened; the Paris-treaty page is silent on it. Counterpart "union-of-soviet-socialist-republics" is the eu-17 dossier. Gazetteer: Dunaujvaros (Dunaújváros, about 18.94 E 46.97 N, a Danube town south of Budapest) is not in places.jsonl, so the dossier uses a 20 km coordinate radius.
